questions.question: Explain how to choose between a bar graph, a histogram and a line graph for a new dataset, giving the test applied to the horizontal axis.
questions.expected_answer: Ask what the horizontal axis carries. Named separate groups (pie types, provinces) take a bar graph with gaps — nothing exists between categories. Numerical intervals tiling a continuous number line (marks 0–9, 10–19) take a histogram with touching bars. A quantity measured repeatedly over time takes a line or broken-line graph with points joined in time order.

questions.question: Chicken holds 40% of the pies pie chart. Calculate its slice angle, and the number of chicken pies if 150 pies are sold in the same proportions, naming the 'whole' used in each calculation.
questions.expected_answer: Angle: the whole is the 360-degree circle, so 0,40 × 360 = 144 degrees. Amount: the whole is the 150 pies, so 0,40 × 150 = 60 chicken pies. Same fraction, two different wholes; shares must total 100% and angles 360 degrees as a check.

questions.question: Using the takings data (340, 430, 120, 450, 490), give the three-layer interpretation: facts, trend, and a supported reason for the exception.
questions.expected_answer: Facts: lowest R120 on Wednesday, highest R490 on Friday, range R370, total R1 830. Trend: rising across the week — Friday is R150 above Monday. Exception with reason: Wednesday breaks the trend; a plausible, data-supported reason is a power cut leaving the warmers cold, so no hot pies could be sold.
